en: The Scripture on the Eight Great Bodhisattvas Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperial Censor of the Third Rank, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of Enlightened Teaching, Subject Faxian, by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Buddha was staying in Śrāvastī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, together with a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus. There were also eight great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who served as the leaders, namely:

the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ārya Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha.
Furthermore, there were great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, whose names were:

the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Aparājita, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Nāgākāra, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Priyadarśana, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Vimalagarbha, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Vimalakīrti, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Jñānarāja, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Anantanandin, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Jñānaprabha, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Prajñāprabha, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Prajñādīpa, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Jñānadīpa, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Brahmadatta, and the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Devamakuṭa.
All such great bodhisattvas as these had come to the assembly and were seated.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śāriputra:
"Listen now with close attention."

Passing beyond worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges to the east, there is a buddha-field named Invincible. In that land dwells a Buddha named Śubhavīryaśrī Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently teaches the subtle and wondrous Dharma to sentient beings.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra! Again, passing ten *gaṅgā*-sands of worlds to the east, there is a buddha-field named Anātman. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Samantaprabhāsa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently preaches the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the sake of sentient beings."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Beyond the worlds to the east, as numerous as the sands of three *gaṅgā* rivers, there is a buddha-field named Sukhāvatī. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Śrī Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently teaches the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the sake of sentient beings."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Again, passing thirty-four worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges to the east, there is a buddha-field named Śāntigarbha. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Indraketudhvajarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently preaches the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the sake of sentient beings."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Beyond five *gaṅgā*-river-sands of worlds to the east, there is a buddha-field named Free from Dust (*Vigataraja*). In that land there is a Buddha, titled Joyful Merit Light Sovereign King Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently preaches the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the sake of sentient beings."
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

"If there are sons or daughters of good family who, upon hearing the names of these Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, within this sutra, listen with single-minded attention, or recollect them themselves, or write them down, read and recite them, or explain them to others, those people at the end of their lives shall not fall into the evil realms; they shall not be born in border regions, among those with wrong views, among those with improper conduct, or within low-born clans; nor shall they be born among the long-lived devas, nor in the five turbidities, nor during the kalpas of famine, disease, or warfare; nor shall they encounter the calamities of kings, water, fire, bandits, or tigers and wolves."

They shall be constantly reborn in Buddha-fields, as well as among devas and humans, with physical forms that are upright and majestic, their sense faculties complete, and their retinues perfect. They shall attain the knowledge of past lives, fulfill the six pāramitās, practice the four immeasurable dharmas, penetrate all profound treasuries of the Dharma, and realize the supreme path.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the great bodhisattvas, Śāriputra, and all the bhikṣus, as well as the devas, humans, asuras, and others, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Eight Great Bodhisattvas
